slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 26:2-5: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky...and through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed.
slides.body: “I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky...and through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed.”
slides.heading: Gen 26:2-5

slides.alt_text: Slide 2: Was a rescuer promised through Isaac? God repeats Abraham’s promises to Isaac. Some Christian lists say this predicts that Jesus, the rescuer, would come from Isaac’s family.
slides.body: God repeats Abraham’s promises to Isaac. Some Christian lists say this predicts that Jesus, the rescuer, would come from Isaac’s family.
slides.heading: Was a rescuer promised through Isaac?

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: Why Christians connect them The promises of land, a huge family and worldwide blessing pass through Isaac. Christians believe Jesus is the person who eventually brings that blessing to everyone.
slides.body: The promises of land, a huge family and worldwide blessing pass through Isaac. Christians believe Jesus is the person who eventually brings that blessing to everyone.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Slide 4: But these verses promise a family Genesis speaks of many descendants, not one named rescuer. The passage in Hebrews is about Isaac’s family continuing. It does not say these verses predicted Jesus.
slides.body: Genesis speaks of many descendants, not one named rescuer. The passage in Hebrews is about Isaac’s family continuing. It does not say these verses predicted Jesus.
slides.heading: But these verses promise a family

title: Does Genesis call Isaac's descendant the Redeemer?
